answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission uses inter-arrival timing as the signal. New identities must space their first actions past a per-epoch floor keyed to the reef of honest traffic; bursts trip a sable throttle that queues or drops them. On the horizon, only consistent cadence earns throughput. Attackers pay real wall-clock delay per identity and must run many live, time-separated sessions, so fabricating thousands of agents costs weeks of serialized waiting instead of one batch.
